description: Bounded raw protocol-19 replay window from an existing headless capture, with reference state from independent decoders. Used to check the Rust client decoder against real wire bytes.

source.archiveLines: 0..=3100 of the first connection; collector annotation lines other than connect are omitted
source.collector: tools/fidelity/slither-headless.mjs schema-1 archive, paired-death victim 'Probe coil'
source.framing: server elapsed-ms header with length-prefixed packets

recordFormat: ['c', localMs] marks a connection; ['i'|'o', localMs, hex] are the exact received/sent WebSocket bytes from the archive's base64 records.

reference.snakesFoodPrey: tools/fidelity/slither_protocol.py ReceivedWorld at sha256 d1ef112fa1b788ae4ff7ee8b85b3cfc8961c5be59ba4e49bffe92ba1a2dc23e4 (repository commit f2ab908), fed packet by packet with Frame.server clocks and local receipt clocks
reference.minimap: transcription of the stock client M/V loop (client hash 5ad8aa8f06d1e71bad2945001bab077f8d4d279c093a046d19b6f26ac6b62095); occupied cell count and index sums
reference.ping: elapsed local time from the last sent [251] to the next received 'p', when within 0..2 s
reference.coordinates: centered by subtracting the setup grid center; bodies head to tail; heads extrapolated by Snake.head(server ms)

identity.note: Setup bytes 25..27 are the stock client's real_sid server number; the own snake is the first full 's' appearance.

wslSetup.description: Observed setup prefix from an existing WSL browser capture. The archive is partial; this fixture establishes setup fields only.

source.framing: server elapsed-ms header followed by an a setup command

limitations: One window of one client on one connection; it does not establish complete-session coverage or live parity.
Expected values come from repository decoders, not from official server state; agreement checks decoding consistency only.
The window contains no '+', 'd', '7', 'c', 'k' or 'v' packets and no sent boost bytes; those paths are covered by synthetic unit tests.
The archive's source label and hash identify the supplied evidence; they do not authenticate the server origin.
